title: Is rotor cant just a cheap way to buy yaw authority that bigger motors would buy as well?
lede: does rotor cant still help once motor headroom is a design variable? With thrust-to-weight free in 1.5–4 (no cant picks the 4.0 ceiling), cant to 35° still beats no cant in 5 of 5 seeds at each of three measured propeller c values, by 1.6–3.4°; headroom alone recovers 2.5–3.5° of the 3.8–4.7° the parent credited to cant.
summary: Follow-up to codesign-aero-cant-propdata (next step: compare at equal cost with a motor upgrade). Thrust-to-weight (motor headroom, 1.5–4.0) becomes an optional design variable beside arm length, propeller size, cant and six PID gains; κ = c D with c at the 10th, 50th and 90th percentile of measured UIUC static propeller data (0.065, 0.081, 0.13). Four arms, 1920 CMA-ES evaluations, 5 seeds, 64 held-out episodes, $300 cost cap. Without cant, free headroom cuts the held-out error from 17.2/17.1/16.1° to 14.7/14.0/12.6° (5 of 5 seeds at every c) but the optimiser sits on the 4.0 ceiling, so these are lower bounds on what headroom buys. With headroom free, cant to 35° still improves it to 11.3/11.2/11.0° (better in 5 of 5, by 3.4, 2.8 and 1.6°); the chosen cant falls from 35° to 23–29° and TWR is 3.7–3.8. At the largest c, cant with TWR 2 is only 0.3° better than no cant with free TWR. Limits: the TWR range, the motor mass/cost fits and plant ranges are assumed, TWR ceiling binds for no cant, attitude steps only, no position hold, no hardware.
